key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The subcutaneous node was first noticed 10 years ago
The node has been slowly growing
The patient experienced swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
The patient experienced mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
A solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque is present in the right axilla
Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells are diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Imaging studies show no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

raw.rationale: The presence of tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, arranged in an 'Indian file pattern', along with positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, is highly suggestive of metastatic invasive lobular breast carcinoma. The history of swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy and episodic pain during menstrual cycles also supports a possible breast origin for the tumor.

rejected.label: invasive lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor is located in the axilla, which is not a typical location for primary invasive lobular carcinoma.

rejected.label: accessory axillary breast tissue
rejected.why: The presence of malignant tumor cells and the pattern of infiltration are not consistent with benign accessory breast tissue.

rejected.label: apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: While the tumor expresses apocrine markers such as GCDFP15 and GATA3, the overall histological and immunohistochemical profile is more consistent with metastatic invasive lobular breast carcinoma.

rejected.label: hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's histological features and immunohistochemical profile do not support a diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma, which typically expresses sweat gland markers and has a different morphological appearance.
